root_cause: The MutationObserver's checkDomRemoval function only checks if the focused node is directly in the removedNodes list. When a parent element (like <li>) is removed, the focused button inside it is not directly in removedNodes, so the trap fails to detect the removal and doesn't restore focus into the dialog.
repair_strategy: Modify checkDomRemoval to also check if any removed node contains the focused node (using Node.contains), so that removal of an ancestor element triggers focus restoration.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus remains trapped inside the dialog after a row containing the focused button is removed, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order) by preventing focus loss to the page body.
functional_risks: Minimal: only adds a contains() check on the focused node's ancestor chain.
No change to focus order, initial focus, or escape behavior.
verification_requirements: Run the frozen journey: open dialog, Tab to first remove button, Enter to remove row, verify focus stays in dialog (#basket:focus-within).
Verify Tab wraps to next focusable element inside dialog.
Verify Shift+Tab wraps backward inside dialog.
Verify Escape key closes dialog and returns focus to trigger button.
